A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same Profile-to-PEFT study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A–K are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalization benchmarks, efficiency measurements, robustness tests and ablations in Sections 5–6, with additional experiments and qualitative examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, analysis figures and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same profile encoding, position-conditioned hypernetwork, LoRA generation, supervised training objective and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LaMP, LongLaMP, Personal Reddit and Empathetic Conversation tasks, including the same random and out-of-distribution user scenarios. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and 6–7 retain their respective comparator sets, including RAG, PAG, Full History, MT-LoRA and OPPU in the main benchmark comparisons. Efficiency comparisons and qualitative examples also retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Data splits, sample counts, metrics, model sizes, training budgets, retrieval settings and decoding procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and the experimental appendices.

E4.justification: The user-diversity, training-quantity, embedding-model, history-length and component analyses are unchanged. Appendices A, B and K retain the same retrieval sensitivity study, smaller-model evaluation and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is unchanged throughout both PDFs. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: All reported scores, timings, rankings, plotted trends and qualitative outputs match, including Tables 1–7, Figures 3–6 and the examples in Tables 9–10.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, LoRA equations, profile-to-parameter mapping and training objective in Sections 2–3 are unchanged, as are the baseline formulations in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about instant personalization, elimination of deployment-time per-user training, generalization, efficiency and local privacy-preserving deployment.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning user diversity, profile summaries and generalization are identical. The single-task-per-user and LoRA-focused limitations, along with the privacy, bias and accessibility discussion, are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation link, hyperparameters, hardware, software, split construction and prompt templates are unchanged. The added corresponding-author contact provides no new technical or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the reference list are identical. The positioning relative to existing personalization methods and hypernetwork-based adaptation is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author designation and contact footnote for Qingkai Zeng on page 1, plus an Acknowledgements section on page 9. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote causes slight text reflow across pages 1–2, and acknowledgements occupy additional space on page 9. All other rendered pages, including every table and appendix page, are identical; figures and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds author-contact and funding acknowledgements, providing administrative completeness. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and substantive readability remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
